quotes.name: Austin Reaves
quotes.quote: To be honest, I'm not really sure about The Reaves Line Transit Fund's impact on Temescal. I founded it, but I've been focused on the A's and family stuff lately. I know it's been around since C109, and it's still active, but I haven't been keeping up with its day-to-day. I live in West Oakland, so I don't really see its effects firsthand.

quotes.name: Brie Harris
quotes.quote: Having my own place in Temescal is still a game-changer for me. It's been nice to have a spot to unwind after being on my feet all day at the flower shop. I feel like I'm still getting used to it, but it's made me appreciate the neighborhood even more.

quotes.name: Helena Voss-Adeyemi
quotes.quote: I walked north across the Temescal line and watched the storefronts change. It's always interesting to see the different vibes on either side. Temescal's got a unique energy, lots of new businesses popping up.

quotes.name: Theo Park
quotes.quote: To be honest, that moment at Temescal Brewing really stuck with me. Seeing the janitor from the Islamic Center chatting with Danny Horn like they were old friends... it felt like a small but real sign of how the neighborhood is evolving. It's not just about new faces moving in; it's about how we all connect. I still see Temescal as a place where you can bump into anyone, and that's something I appreciate.
